Implement a user-facing registration form with validation and confirmation steps to allow users to create accounts independently. (Self Registration) Allows users to create their own accounts in the system without administrative intervention.

Use a standard authentication mechanism that verifies user credentials against stored data during login. (Authentication) Manages user identity verification typically through credentials like ID and password.

Implement a secure credential storage system with encryption and access controls to protect user passwords and related data. (Credential Store) A secure storage system for user credentials such as passwords and authentication tokens.

Implement a Facade that abstracts the interaction with the maps provider(s) to allow users to find pick-up locations easily, hiding complexity and enabling future extensibility. (Facade) Provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem, such as integrating multiple map providers or location services into a single unified API for the user.

Use Adapter to integrate different map providers by adapting their interfaces to a common one used by the system. (Adapter) Converts the interface of a maps provider or location service into one that the system expects, allowing integration of different map APIs with varying interfaces.

Implement Strategy pattern to allow switching between different map providers or search algorithms dynamically. (Strategy) Defines a family of algorithms (e.g., different map providers or location search strategies) and makes them interchangeable at runtime.

Implement MVC to manage user interactions for viewing order history, browsing promotions, and subscription plans, ensuring a clean separation between UI and data logic. (Model View Controller) Separates the application into three interconnected components: Model (data), View (UI), and Controller (business logic).

Use Repository pattern to abstract data access for orders, promotions, and subscriptions, supporting MVC's Model component. (Repository) Provides a centralized abstraction for data access, encapsulating storage and retrieval logic.

Apply Observer pattern to notify views of changes in promotions or subscription plans to keep UI updated. (Observer) Defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

Use MVC to handle user interactions for profile updates, meal order modifications, browsing meals, and displaying detailed meal information, ensuring a clean separation between UI and business logic. (Model View Controller) Separates the application into three interconnected components: Model (data), View (UI), and Controller (business logic).

Implement repositories for user profiles, meal orders, and meals to manage data operations and queries efficiently. (Repository) Provides a centralized abstraction for data access, encapsulating storage, retrieval, and query logic.

Use specifications to implement meal search filters and criteria for availability and dietary needs. (Specification) Encapsulates business rules or criteria that can be combined to query or filter objects.
